text: The Bengaluru Heat Collective was launched in Bengaluru on 15 July 2026 by 11 organisations, as a platform to advance coordinated action on rising urban heat.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: WRI India published its launch release on 17 July 2026, two days after the event.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: The 11 founding members named at launch: ARTPARK, Bengaluru Sustainability Forum, C40 Cities, CSTEP, Hasiru Dala, HeatWatch, Jan Sahas, KHPT, NIMHANS, Socratus and WRI India.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: KHPT's announcement gives fuller names for several members: C40 Cities South and West Asia, Center for Study of Science, Technology and Policy, Jan Sahas Foundation, NIMHANS, Bangalore, and Socratus Collective Wisdom Corporation; it describes KHPT as a founding partner.

sources.label: KHPT: KHPT Joins 10 Organisations to Launch the Bengaluru Heat Collective, 2026

text: KHPT posted its announcement on 17 July 2026.

sources.label: KHPT: KHPT Joins 10 Organisations to Launch the Bengaluru Heat Collective, 2026

text: For its initial phase the Collective named four priority areas: understanding heat and its spatial dimensions to inform policy and investment; enabling infrastructure interventions; strengthening relief and resilience measures for vulnerable communities; and advancing ward-level microplanning.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: KHPT describes the same four areas as mapping heat risk across the city, building cooling infrastructure such as shade, shelters and hydration points, strengthening health monitoring and protections for outdoor and informal workers, and developing ward level microplans.

sources.label: KHPT: KHPT Joins 10 Organisations to Launch the Bengaluru Heat Collective, 2026

text: At the launch, an ASHA worker, a domestic worker, a construction worker and a waste picker spoke about heat in their work.

sources.label: KHPT: KHPT Joins 10 Organisations to Launch the Bengaluru Heat Collective, 2026

text: Officials of Bengaluru North City Corporation, Bengaluru South City Corporation and NIUA's Climate Centre for Cities spoke at the launch.

sources.label: KHPT: KHPT Joins 10 Organisations to Launch the Bengaluru Heat Collective, 2026

text: On 14 July 2026 the city observatory recorded 33.6°C, which WRI India, citing the India Meteorological Department, describes as Bengaluru's highest July temperature on record, above 33.3°C set in 1914 and 1926.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: At the launch, the Commissioner of Bengaluru North City Corporation referred to ₹5 crore allocated for heat resilience by an NIUA pilot, under the Building Heat Resilient Cities Programme of AMRUT 2.0. The figure is attributed to that statement; no sanction order was found.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: Of that ₹5 crore, ₹1 crore was described as dedicated to protecting vulnerable populations, such as safety gear for outdoor informal workers. It is part of the ₹5 crore, not an addition to it.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: NIUA's Climate Centre for Cities said the heat resilience proposal was submitted by Bengaluru North City Corporation.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: The Commissioner described roof coating demonstrations on North City Corporation buildings as planned. No completed installation was found reported.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: An independent report of the launch says the ₹1 crore would go to safety gear and neck fans for outdoor informal workers, and mentions albedo coating demonstrations.

sources.label: The Chenab Times: Bengaluru Heat Collective Launched to Combat Rising Temperatures, 2026

text: Bengaluru South City Corporation (BSCC) announced ₹2 crore allocated for phased implementation of the Begur Ward Climate Action Plan, covering heat proofing of buildings, blue-green schools and groundwater recharge, and its Chief Engineer called it not a final budget but a starting point. Not all of it is heat-specific.

sources.label: WRI India: Eleven Organisations Launch Bengaluru Heat Collective as City Records its Highest July Temperature at 33.6°C, 2026

text: WRI India's partner update of 27 June 2026 reports that four of the five municipal corporations allocated about ₹52 crore in total directly towards climate action in their 2026-27 budgets. This is climate spending in general, not heat spending.

sources.label: WRI India on Rainmatter Grove: Transforming India's City Regions: partner updates, 2026

text: Ward-level climate action plans are led by the Bengaluru Climate Action Cell under the Greater Bengaluru Authority, with five pilot wards, one per zone: Shantinagar, Jakkur, Begur, Vijinapura and Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar. Public consultations were held in all five.

sources.label: Mongabay India: Ward-level plans bring climate action closer to communities, 2026

text: Heat is not one of the plans' seven sectors; local heat maps were among the data gathered, and residents mapped cool spaces in Jakkur.

sources.label: Mongabay India: Ward-level plans bring climate action closer to communities, 2026

text: Mongabay India reported in March 2026 that the older administrative body had allocated ₹28 crore for climate action and that the new zone-wise budgets were yet to be released; Citizen Matters described the same ₹28 crore as earmarked in the 2025-26 budget for proposed ward-level plans.

sources.label: Mongabay India: Ward-level plans bring climate action closer to communities, 2026
Citizen Matters: Bengaluru is building ward-level climate action plans: Here is how, 2025

text: Citizen Matters lists a seven-organisation working group: WRI India, Socratus Foundation, Jansahas, WellLabs, Sensing Local, CSTEP and Hasiru Dala, and reports plans for ten wards across five city corporations, starting with Shantinagar.

sources.label: Citizen Matters: Bengaluru is building ward-level climate action plans: Here is how, 2025

text: Mongabay India describes WELL Labs as a technical partner for the city climate plan and CSTEP as anchoring the energy sector for the ward plans.

sources.label: Mongabay India: Ward-level plans bring climate action closer to communities, 2026

text: ARTPARK, a not-for-profit company at IISc, describes sub-district heat-risk predictions up to seven days ahead, built with the Government of Karnataka (KSNDMC, KSDMA and the Department of Health). The page gives no public access link, users or accuracy figures.

sources.label: ARTPARK (AI & Robotics Technology Park), IISc: Social impact programmes, 2026

where: Tool: BHRIGU National Heat Insights Explorer
text: CSTEP's BHRIGU project describes an open-access National Heat Insights Explorer for multi-hazard risk visualisation, and phased work in six representative urbanscapes, as outcomes envisioned. The page names neither the six places nor a live address.

sources.label: CSTEP: Building Heat Resilience in India's Growing Urbanscapes (BHRIGU), 2025

text: CSTEP is conducting an organisational mapping exercise of actors engaged in building heat resilience in India; this profile used it as a discovery source and checked each entry separately.

sources.label: CSTEP: Building Heat Resilience in India's Growing Urbanscapes (BHRIGU), 2025

text: CSTEP is developing an Ecosystem-based Adaptation Feasibility Tool (DEFT) for Bengaluru, extending to Bangalore Urban District, supported by IUCN under the Global EbA Fund; intended outputs include hyper-local flood and heatwave risk mapping and a blue-green infrastructure map. The page also reports a household survey across Bangalore. No live tool address is given.

sources.label: CSTEP: Developing an Ecosystem-based Adaptation Feasibility Tool (DEFT), 2025

text: CSTEP held a stakeholder engagement workshop for DEFT using Hebbal as a case study.

sources.label: CSTEP: Developing an Ecosystem-based Adaptation Feasibility Tool (DEFT), 2025

text: HeatWatch has an interactive dashboard combining temperature data with factory-level insights from India's textile and garment sector, mapping brand supply chains. A Bengaluru deployment was not found: its garment fieldwork named elsewhere is outside Bengaluru.

sources.label: HeatWatch: HeatWatch India, 2026

where: Tool: Heat Safety Charter for apartment workers
text: The Bangalore Apartment Federation and HeatWatch Foundation developed a Heat Safety Charter for Apartment Workers, with support from the Bangalore Sustainability Forum, setting out heat safety measures apartment communities can adopt, in English, Kannada and Hindi. No adoption figures were found.

sources.label: HeatWatch: Heat Safety Charter for Workers in Apartments, 2026

where: Tool: Heat Safety Charter for apartment workers
text: The charter's measures can also support security guards, housekeeping staff, gardeners, delivery workers and drivers at apartment complexes.

sources.label: HeatWatch: Heat Safety Charter for Workers in Apartments, 2026

text: A survey of 154 waste workers in Bengaluru (98 women and 56 men) by HeatWatch and Hasiru Dala found only 39.6% had access to clean drinking water and 13% to clean washrooms; free-roaming waste pickers lost an average of ₹504 a week, about 14% of income, and reported ₹1,196 a month in medical costs for heat-related illness.

sources.label: HeatWatch and Hasiru Dala: Rising Heat and Waste Workers: Impact of Heat Stress on the Livelihood and Health of Waste Workers in Bengaluru, 2025

text: Over 60% of respondents belonged to Scheduled Castes, and over 92% said heat makes their tasks harder and slower.

sources.label: HeatWatch and Hasiru Dala: Rising Heat and Waste Workers: Impact of Heat Stress on the Livelihood and Health of Waste Workers in Bengaluru, 2025

text: HeatWatch and volunteers audited parks closed between 11 AM and 4 PM and, in April 2026, asked for park hours of 5 AM to 10 PM and for parks to be treated as cooling and resting spaces. No decision was found reported.

sources.label: HeatWatch: #OpenOurParks: keeping Bengaluru's parks open when it matters most, 2026

text: HeatWatch has begun engaging with domestic workers in Bengaluru with the Domestic Workers Union, as an ongoing area of work.

sources.label: HeatWatch: Domestic workers, 2026

text: A domestic-worker heat stress project by HeatWatch Foundation with St John's Medical College Hospital, listed among Bengaluru Sustainability Forum's supported projects, started in September 2025, with participatory research, workshops and a playbook for other cities among its planned outputs.

sources.label: Bengaluru Sustainability Forum: Addressing heat stress among domestic workers in Bangalore, 2025

text: Bengaluru Sustainability Forum describes itself as an inter-institutional initiative; its Small Grants Programme, started in 2018, has funded over 40 projects.

sources.label: Bengaluru Sustainability Forum: Bengaluru Sustainability Forum, 2026

text: With a Global Resilience Partnership award, Socratus co-designed focus group discussions with Bengaluru Sustainability Forum under its Climate Charche initiative, with domestic, gig and migrant workers, pourakarmikas and ASHA workers; water was the central theme and heat a secondary one.

sources.label: Global Resilience Partnership: Art for Resilience in Bengaluru, 2025

text: The Migrants Resilience Collaborative, initiated by Jan Sahas, ran three cooling centres in Bengaluru in 2026, at a construction site in Whitefield, in Greater Bengaluru Authority facilities in Vidyaranyapura and above an Anganwadi in Allalasandra, open from 10 April to the first week of July, with drinking water, ORS, coolers, cots and first aid.

sources.label: The Migration Story: Air coolers, ORS and medical aid: Outdoor workers in India find rare relief from heat, 2026

text: Staff at the Vidyaranyapura centre told the reporter it helped more than 10 workers apply for construction welfare cards and around 60 to register for Ayushman and e-Shram benefits.

sources.label: The Migration Story: Air coolers, ORS and medical aid: Outdoor workers in India find rare relief from heat, 2026

text: Writing for the India Climate Collaborative, the Migrants Resilience Collaborative reports a study of over 2,300 migrant households in which 89% named heat as the main stressor, and says cooling access was first piloted in Bengaluru.

sources.label: India Climate Collaborative (blog by Migrants Resilience Collaborative): Centering workers in heat resilience: from lived experience to systemic action, 2026

text: In April 2026, Hasiru Dala, C40 Cities and Sensing Local gave cooling kits to 202 workers, including 46 ASHAs, 116 pourakarmikas, 18 dry waste collection centre workers and 20 traffic police, mostly in the North City Corporation. Each kit cost about ₹2,160; an impact report was being prepared.

sources.label: Citizen Matters: Cooling kits help Bengaluru workers combat heat stress, 2026

text: The project team proposed activating 63 Indira canteens across all five city corporations as public cooling centres during heat alerts; scale-up was to use funds under the national heat resilience programme of MoHUA and NIUA. Both are proposals.

sources.label: Citizen Matters: Cooling kits help Bengaluru workers combat heat stress, 2026

text: C40 Cities sought technical assistance, with proposals due on 19 October 2025, to develop two High Impact Actions with detailed project reports for urban heat in identified wards of Bengaluru, working with the Greater Bengaluru Authority over about five months from November 2025.

sources.label: C40 Cities: Request for Proposals: Development of High Impact Actions for Heat Resilience in Bengaluru and Hubballi-Dharwad, 2025
